page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores using the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on external storage solutions. Network connectivity is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor architecture provides a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector calculations and machine learning inference tasks. Cryptographic operations are assisted by hardware-level AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth present certain tradeoffs. While large-block memory read and write speeds align with average tiering, small-block cached memory read bandwidth and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving benchmarks are positioned in the lower performance quartile.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and high single-core performance relative to its resource footprint, the ecs.c8ae.xlarge offers a specialized hardware profile for compute-bound tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity. This makes the instance suitable for single-threaded processing, text processing, and lightweight computational workloads. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or parallelized compilation tasks due to the observed memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling limitations.
